newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGB futures end lower on last-minute profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: JGB futures end lower on last-minute profit-taking.

text.p: Key June Japanese government bond (JGB) futures ended Tuesday's Tokyo session down on profit-taking, hedge selling and loss-cut liquidation of longs, traders said.
The June closed down 0.19 at 127.00. Turnover was 46,839.
The key contract was firmer in the mid-afternoon on talk that today's 20-year government bond auction would produce strong results.
After the auction results were announced at 2.30 p.m. (0530 GMT), profit-taking and hedge selling emerged, traders said.
The June fell as low as 126.98 shortly before the close.
The auction of 3.0 percent 400 billion yen 20-year JGBs produced a lowest price of 100.50 and an average price of 100.53, the Ministry of Finance said.

"A strong auction had been widely expected. A 3.0 coupon helped to attract more regional investors to the new 20-year bonds. Earlier in the day, some players had been expecting a 2.9 percent coupon," said a brokerage house trader.
Traders said investors continued to show strong appetite for cash JGBs, particularly at the long-end of the yield curve.
"Investor demand for the 190th to 194th JGBs was very strong," said a trader at another brokerage house.

In the morning session, the June futures set an all-time high of 127.34, but pared gains by midday following remarks by a government minister urging the Bank of Japan (BOJ) to consider raising interest rates.
Kabun Muto, director-general of the Management and Coordination Agency, urged the BOJ to consider the possibility of raising the official discount rate, a spokesman for the agency said on Tuesday.
"The impact was short-lived as the market did not take Muto too seriously. A near-term BOJ tightening is quite unlikely," said a trader at a trust bank's securities unit.
The yen's weakness and a rise in Tokyo stocks were also responsible for capping JGBs' upside, traders said.

The dollar rose as high as 126.12 yen in the Tokyo afternoon, compared with Monday's New York close of 125.60/65 yen. The Nikkei 225 stock average closed up 306.03 points, or 1.73 percent, at 18,021.70.
"Some JGB players withdrew bids after seeing the Nikkei rise above 18,000," said the first trader.
A massive amount of new corporate straight bonds launched on Monday and Tuesday was also making JGBs' upside heavy, traders said.

"A total of about 300 billion worth of new corporate straight bonds was launched on Monday and Tuesday alone. The market would need time to digest all these new offerings," said the trader at a trust bank's securities unit.

The yield of the benchmark cash 182nd JGB stood at 2.100 percent as of 4.30 p.m. (0730 GMT), up from 2.095 percent on Monday. It fell as low as 2.075 percent in the mid-afternoon, setting a record low yield for any benchmark 10-year JGB.
